mechanism_narrative: Broad out-of-home activity is contracting: TRANSIT, WORKPLACES, and PARKS all fell in the latest week, which reduces incidental retail and recreation footfall; therefore RETAIL_REC over the next four weeks will be lower than its last four-week mean.
evidence_refs: fact:TRANSIT fell from -9.6 to -11.7 in t-0w
failure_condition: If RETAIL_REC over the next 28 days is equal to or higher than its last 28-day mean when TRANSIT, WORKPLACES, and PARKS all decline in the latest week.

mechanism_narrative: A TRANSIT drop below -10 percent change from baseline signals a behavioral shift away from discretionary trips; when this threshold is crossed, retail and recreation visits decline further over the next week.
failure_condition: If RETAIL_REC over the next 28 days rises above its last 28-day mean when TRANSIT is below -10.

mechanism_narrative: PARKS and GROCERY_PHARM interact: a sharp PARKS decline combined with positive GROCERY_PHARM indicates households are cutting outdoor leisure but still making essential trips, leaving less scope for retail recreation, so RETAIL_REC falls over the next two weeks.
evidence_refs: fact:PARKS dropped from 4.9 to -6.7 in t-0w while GROCERY_PHARM stayed at 4.0
failure_condition: If the combination of PARKS below 0 and GROCERY_PHARM above 0 during the latest week is followed by RETAIL_REC equal to or above its last 28-day mean.

mechanism_narrative: The onset of the early-summer rainy season reduces PARKS visits, and this outdoor avoidance redirects some discretionary spending into indoor retail and recreation, lifting RETAIL_REC over the next two weeks.
candidate_trigger: PARKS falls below 0 percent change from baseline
evidence_refs: fact:PARKS fell from 4.9 to -6.7 in t-0w
failure_condition: If RETAIL_REC over the next 28 days is equal to or lower than its last 28-day mean when PARKS is below 0 in the latest week.

mechanism_narrative: RESIDENTIAL mobility remains near zero and GROCERY_PHARM stays positive, indicating no renewed stay-at-home wave and continued essential shopping; this normalization supports a gradual recovery in RETAIL_REC over the next four weeks.
evidence_refs: fact:RESIDENTIAL is 0.1 and GROCERY_PHARM is 4.0 at t-0w
failure_condition: If RETAIL_REC over the next 28 days is equal to or lower than its last 28-day mean while RESIDENTIAL is near zero and GROCERY_PHARM is positive.

mechanism_narrative: WORKPLACES below -12 percent change from baseline reflects sustained remote-work or office-avoidance policy; continued workplace absence drains downtown lunchtime and after-work retail traffic, pushing RETAIL_REC lower over the next four weeks.
failure_condition: If RETAIL_REC over the next 28 days is equal to or higher than its last 28-day mean when WORKPLACES is at or below -12 in the latest week.

mechanism_narrative: TRANSIT and RESIDENTIAL interact: when TRANSIT falls while RESIDENTIAL stays near zero, the mobility reduction is driven by fewer discretionary trips rather than staying home, which depresses RETAIL_REC over the next week.
evidence_refs: fact:TRANSIT is -11.7 and RESIDENTIAL is 0.1 at t-0w
failure_condition: If the interaction of TRANSIT below -10 and RESIDENTIAL at or below 0.5 is followed by RETAIL_REC equal to or above its last 28-day mean.

mechanism_narrative: GROCERY_PHARM has fallen from 7.0 to 4.0, signaling the end of a pantry-stocking phase; reduced grocery trips remove a complementary driver of nearby retail traffic, so RETAIL_REC declines over the next two weeks.
candidate_trigger: GROCERY_PHARM falls more than 2 points week-on-week
evidence_refs: fact:GROCERY_PHARM fell from 7.0 at t-2w to 4.0 at t-0w
failure_condition: If RETAIL_REC over the next 28 days is equal to or higher than its last 28-day mean after GROCERY_PHARM falls more than 2 points week-on-week.
